learning: No race data yet. Tune base_speed first if the completion time is the limit, and kp/kd if steering_oscillation or max_error is high on the slalom.
notes: Baseline geometry with a conservative controller: kp 3, kd 0.3, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.4, last_direction line-loss recovery. The full measurement set is requested so the first race shows which objective term limits the score.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so the controller is a conservative starting point for the Builder's baseline geometry. Geometry is kept as proposed: five forward sensors at x = 0.04, 0.02, 0, -0.02, -0.04 m and y = 0.04 m, 12 mm footprints, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.8 kg, 0.16 m body length and 0.12 m body width. All values are inside the contract limits. Sensor weights are [2, 1, 0, -1, -2] to match the sensor x order, so a line on the left (positive x) gives a positive signal, which steers left. The signal is bounded at |2|, so kp = 3 gives a turn of up to about 6 units (about 2100 PWM counts) at full deflection, which is firm but not saturating on the 0.12 m track. kd = 0.3 damps the response on the slalom without much noise amplification. ki = 0.05 is small, since the signal is already centred on the line and the integral can wind up on the motor mismatch. base_speed = 1.4 gives about 70 percent PWM. That is the main unknown: the course needs about 1.5 m/s average to finish in 3 s, so this may be slightly low or may overshoot on the slalom. line_loss = last_direction returns the robot toward the side it left the tape, which suits a sensor array ahead of the axle. The observation request covers completion, progress, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events, oscillation, control effort, controller errors and noise robustness, so the next race will show which term is limiting. Expected result is completion on the oval and s-bend with a few line-loss events, and oscillation on the slalom. This is an estimate, not a measured result.
